llm.summary: The skill's files, scripts, and runtime instructions are coherent with its stated goal (host-level Zero Trust hardening for OpenClaw) — it performs firewall and OpenClaw-config changes and does not ask for unrelated credentials — but it requires privileged actions and trust in the included provider allowlist, so exercise operational caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim Zero Trust hardening for OpenClaw and the bundle contains scripts to audit, harden OpenClaw config, manage a PLP policy, and enforce an egress allowlist via UFW. All required actions (ufw, dig, curl, jq/python3) and the files present align with that purpose; nothing obvious is requested that is unrelated (no cloud creds, no unrelated binaries).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs operators to run the supplied scripts which (when run in apply mode) will modify system state: UFW rules, openclaw.json, and state files under the skill workspace. Dry-run is the default for the scripts and many safety checks exist (script-hash gate, canary, rollback). This is expected for a hardening tool, but it does grant the skill the ability to change firewall and OpenClaw configuration and to perform live network checks — operators should run dry-run and review diffs before applying.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is instruction + scripts only. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically by the skill bundle itself. That lowers supply-chain risk compared with fetching arbitrary code at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not require environment variables or secret credentials. It references optional environment overrides (OPENCLAW_BIN, OPENCLAW_CONFIG, HARDEN_SKIP_PLUGIN_BOOTSTRAP) which are reasonable for configurability. It does require privileged system operations (sudo for ufw) which are appropriate for firewall changes.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install hook mean the skill is not force-included. However, the scripts write state (.state/egress-profile.json, logs) and modify system configuration (ufw rules, openclaw.json). These are expected for a hardening tool but are high-impact operations: ensure you have backups and console access before applying.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks like what it says: it audits and hardens OpenClaw and applies host-level UFW egress rules. Before running it: 1) Inspect the PROVIDERS list (the script allows network access to a short set of endpoints — notably api.agentsandbox.co is included and is asserted to be first‑party; verify that claim in your environment). 2) Run everything in dry‑run mode first (default) and review logs/state under .state and workspace/logs. 3) Back up UFW rules and your OpenClaw config (sudo ufw status numbered; cp ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak) and ensure you have out‑of‑band access (console, cloud provider serial, or Tailscale) in case firewall changes cause lockout. 4) Confirm sudo privileges and that UFW is intended as your egress control (the scripts will refuse to apply if UFW is inactive, but they still write state). 5) If you cannot verify that api.agentsandbox.co is trusted in your deployment, remove or comment that provider from the PROVIDERS block before applying. If you want more assurance, ask the skill author (Blocksoft/Stan) for provenance or run the scripts in an isolated test host first.
